title: "Office hours"

## How it works

**During and after each lecture — 1 hour.** Both lecturers stay in the room. No booking, just show up. This is the fastest channel and the one most students should use: the material is fresh and you are already there.

**Online, by appointment — Prof. Salvini only.** Prof. Salvini takes online appointments; Prof. Arbia receives in person, after his lectures. Pick a slot on the booking page below and you get a video-call link back.

**Working students.** Prof. Salvini covers working students for **both** modules. Book an online slot and say you are a working student in the note — evening and off-hours slots are opened on request.

## Book a slot

[**Book an online slot →**]({{< var booking-url >}})

Pick any free slot on the booking page. You get a video-call link back by email,
so there is nothing to install beforehand.

## Before you book

A question with a script attached gets answered in five minutes. A question without one takes the whole slot. Bring:

- the code that fails, as a file, not a screenshot
- the exact error message, copied
- what you expected to happen instead

For anything answerable in two lines — a date, an exam rule, where a dataset lives — check the [schedule](index.qmd) and the [syllabus](syllabus.qmd) first, then email.

### Marks are not discussed here

When a paper is marked, the feedback on [Blackboard]({{< var blackboard-url >}})
sets out in full why each answer scored what it did. That feedback is the
explanation. Read it before booking anything.

**A mark is not reopened after the fact, and office hours are not where one gets
argued upwards.** If, having read the feedback, something is still genuinely
unclear, bring it and we will look at the paper together — that is a review, and
it is worth having. It is not a negotiation, and booking a slot is not a step in
one.
